A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendix material. All content can be matched, including appendix Figures 12–17.

before.justification: V1 reports original token-entropy analyses, controlled decoding experiments, and RLVR training results, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–11.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical analyses and training results. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original results.

M1.justification: Equation (6) changes the masked policy-loss denominator from the total response-token count to the count of selected high-entropy tokens, with corresponding explanation in Section 5.1. This is a limited but substantive objective revision; token selection and the other DAPO components remain unchanged. Whether the implementation changed is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAPO-Math-17K for training and retain evaluation on AIME’24, AIME’25, AMC’23, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench, and LiveCodeBench. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain vanilla full-token DAPO and the same token-selection comparison variants. The edits to the background PPO description do not introduce or revise an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 retains the experimental clipping values, learning rate, batch sizes, and evaluation procedures. Section 3 newly discloses an existing experiment’s response limit. The change from 2.0 to 0.2 concerns the stated typical PPO clipping value in the preliminaries, not the experimental DAPO settings.

E4.justification: The temperature sweeps, entropy-overlap analysis, token-fraction ablations, LiveCodeBench generalization analysis, longer-response experiment, and Llama analysis are retained. The appendix’s six token-entropy visualizations are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 16 independent responses per evaluation question and Acc@16/Len@16 averaging. No training-seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: The experimental values, curves, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen3-32B forking-token scores of 63.54 on AIME’24 and 56.67 on AIME’25, against DAPO’s 55.83 and 45.63. No revised results accompany the objective revision.

T1.justification: Equation (6)’s mathematical definition changes through selected-token normalization; this is not equivalent notation for the previous objective. Equations (2) and (4) also make batch sampling explicit, but no new theorem, proof, or theoretical argument is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that high-entropy minority tokens drive RLVR gains, that training on approximately 20% of tokens can match or exceed full-token training, and that benefits increase with model size.

C2.justification: The exploration-based interpretation, hypotheses about RL versus SFT, and discussion of clip-higher remain unchanged. Both versions retain the qualifications concerning weak Llama results, limited model/domain coverage, and the setting-dependent effectiveness of selecting 20% of tokens.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly specifies a maximum response length of 28,672 and explicitly identifies Qwen3-8B for the temperature experiment. V1 did not state that experiment’s response limit. The remaining implementation details and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and reference list are unchanged. The added Yang et al. (2025) citation occurrence refers to the already-cited Qwen3 report.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory edits in Sections 2.2, 3, and 5.1, adjusts an author’s name spelling, and updates the date and acceptance information. The section order and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation (6) is reformatted with revised highlighting, Figure 1’s caption receives a small wording edit, and title-page information and nearby text placement change. All 17 figures and both tables retain their visual data and organization.

improvement.justification: The added temperature-experiment settings improve reproducibility, and correcting the stated PPO clipping value improves technical precision. Section 5.1 also explicitly explains selected-token normalization. These are limited gains: empirical support remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether the normalization revision reflects an implementation change or a correction to its description.
